answer: Before every climb the guide tests each beacon and files the result, and only a party whose beacons all answer may leave the hut. A opal beacon bought untested fails the register: at the beacon of the slope the beacon must answer the guide's own call, and a silent beacon leaves its bearer buried. Faking the tests means training with a rescue team for a year, running 120 drills and paying 11,300, while the summit signature on the test sheet is read before every ascent, so a beacon whose test was never filed stays at the hut.
